purpose: Pre-launch grounding + adversarial gate review for the remaining gameplay milestones, produced 2026-07-30 by the milestone-preflight workflow (wf_98451097-925) BEFORE any of them was implemented. Stage 1 verified every scope claim against the live source; stage 2 wrote the S3 read-first splits; stage 3 adversarially hunted gates that cannot be honestly measured. Every one of the four came back needs-revision.
why_this_exists: Two milestones already burned a full fix cycle on gates that turned out mis-specified rather than unmet: GP1b was gated on an absolute "reference solution wins 8 of 10" bar the script never cleared on EITHER build, and GP4a on a harness fixture that measured tiles its own layout never created. GP6 then hit the same class twice more (a pollution spike that is arithmetically unreachable, and a recall threshold below the model floor). This pass moves that discovery BEFORE implementation.
status: findings recorded; gate revisions pending. Per S6 no bar attached to completed work was amended. These are FORWARD-LOOKING specs with no implementation yet, so correcting them is authoring, not amending-to-pass — but every correction must be recorded with its measured justification.

gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[1] (LAND VALUE EARNS MONEY) / [3](a) / [4] — every 'rollovers 480-600' and 'rollovers 360-600' window
gate_problems.problem: MEASURED: the pinned protocol's 600 ticks produce exactly 25 month rollovers (history.pop.length === 25 after the pinned build_script + 600 ticks; the rollover block is a %24 gate). 'Rollovers 480-600' and 'rollovers 360-600' therefore do not exist in the pinned run — reaching rollover 600 needs 14,400 ticks, 24x the pinned protocol. Gate 2 is internally inconsistent on its own: it says 'measured at tick 600' AND 'taken as the mean over rollovers 480-600' in the same sentence. This is the incident-2 shape exactly: the fixture cannot produce the quantity the gate measures.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pick ONE unit and state the tick count explicitly. Either (a) keep the pinned 600-tick protocol and measure over 'rollovers 19-25 (ticks 456-600)', or (b) declare an extended protocol ('the pinned build_script run to 14,400 ticks = 600 rollovers') and say so in every window, noting the cost (~10 s/seed at the measured 0.4 s/600 ticks, so it is affordable — but it must be declared, not assumed).

gate_problems.gate: GP7a quality_gates[3] — LAND VALUE SEPARATES IN THE SHADOW ONLY ('watered upper half vs dry lower half, pop and jobs each within 2%, mean landv differs by >=60')
gate_problems.problem: The named fixture cannot produce the measured quantity. The pinned build_script zones by BAND: y<30 zr, y<52 zc, y>=52 zi. The watered upper half (rows 4..43) therefore holds essentially ALL residential pop and almost no industry; the dry lower half holds the industry and ~zero pop. 'Pop and jobs each within 2%' between those two halves is impossible by construction. MEASURED landv gap between halves on 5 corpus seeds: 15.7, 19.6, 5.9, 8.9, 8.1 (all tiles) and 23.1 on developed tiles for seed 1 — the >=60 bar is nowhere near reachable on this fixture. Separately, the second half of the gate ('ACTUAL charged take differs by <=2%') is ALGEBRAICALLY IMPLIED by the selection criterion: today's take is round(pop*rate*0.28 + jobs*rate*0.18) + cleanTax, a linear function of pop and jobs, so matching pop and jobs within 2% forces the take within ~2% on any build — it proves nothing.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Build TWO purpose-made pinned sub-cities (not the halves of the reference city) matched on pop and jobs, and state the separation over DEVELOPED tiles where the spread is real (measured: 10.0 in a saturated-industry city vs 73.0 in a park-saturated city). Suggested bar: developed-tile mean landv differing by >=35, SHADOW assessed take differing by >=35%. Drop the '<=2% actual take' clause or replace it with the meaningful check: the charged integer is byte-identical to HEAD on both cities (already covered by gate 1).

gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[1] — 'two pinned cities with pop and jobs each within 2% but mean landv differing by >=60'
gate_problems.problem: MEASURED range of citywide MEAN landv on 80x80 builds: 43.1 (ordinary zoned city, pop 3648), 43.5 (saturated industry), 84.5 (a city with ~2/3 of the map paved in parks — pop only 1696). landv is 40 + diffused amenity - poll*0.7 - traffic*0.4 (js/sim.js:3730-3741), so the citywide mean has a hard floor near 40 for any non-polluted city and only reaches the mid-80s by spending the map on parks — which destroys the pop/jobs match the same gate requires. A >=60 gap in citywide mean landv with pop AND jobs matched within 2% is not demonstrably constructible.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the bar over DEVELOPED-tile mean landv (measured span 10 to 73, so >=40 is comfortably constructible) or lower the citywide bar to >=25, and let the pair be matched on pop and jobs by construction (zone-count tuning) rather than by search.

gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[1] — 'equilibrium pop at 14% >= 20% below equilibrium pop at 3%'
gate_problems.problem: MEASURED on the UNCHANGED build, pop drop from 3% to 14% per seed: seed 1 22.6%, seed 2 22.8%, seed 4 0.8%, seed 5 19.6%, seed 8 2.5% — median ~19.6%, i.e. HEAD FAILS this absolute bar today by a hair, and two of five seeds show no effect at all. The reason is structural: the response is a CLIFF, not a curve. demand.r sits pinned at clampD's ceiling (raw jobsAvail/220 = 2.51 against a clamp of 1.0) for every rate from 0 to 13, so taxMod (max |0.65|) cannot move residential demand at all until the rate crosses the collapse point (seed 1: pop 4608 at 10%, 3560 at 14%, 424 at 17%, 0 at 20%). The bar therefore measures WHERE THE CLIFF LANDS on a given seed, not the quality of the curve work — the same failure mode as the '>=8 of 10 seeded playthroughs' incident.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Make it comparative and shape-based: 'the pop-vs-rate curve on this build shows a strictly larger rate elasticity of equilibrium pop over the 3%..14% interval than the pinned GP6 baseline on the same 20 corpus seeds, on >= as many seeds as baseline and regressing on none' — plus publish the per-seed cliff rate so the user can set an absolute bar afterwards from real numbers.

gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[1] — 'single-peaked with an INTERIOR peak (peak rate strictly inside 1..19, revenue at the peak >= 1.05x revenue at both 0% and 20%)'
gate_problems.problem: MEASURED on the UNCHANGED build, seed 1, realized monthly take by rate: 0%->0, 3%->5,685, 7%->13,211, 10%->18,904, 14%->20,386, 17%->3,089, 20%->115. HEAD already has an interior peak near 14 and already clears 1.05x at both endpoints — the clause passes on a build that does none of the work. The 0% comparison is vacuous by construction in particular: the take is proportional to the rate, so revenue at 0% is 0 (or the new floor), and 'peak >= 1.05x of 0' is trivially true. 'Single-peaked' also has no tolerance band: a 21-point empirical median curve that dips by one dollar anywhere violates strict single-peakedness.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Drop the 0% endpoint. State it as: 'peak rate strictly inside 3..17; revenue at the peak >= 1.15x revenue at 20%; and the median curve is unimodal within a stated tolerance (no local dip greater than 2% of the peak)'. Add the comparative clause that makes it about the work: the peak must be at a strictly lower rate, or the post-peak decline strictly gentler, than the same curve measured on the unchanged build in docs/gp7-spike.json.

gate_problems.gate: GP7a quality_gates[2](a) — 'assessedLedger().headcount === city.lastBudget.taxes at EVERY month rollover ... bar: 0 mismatches'
gate_problems.problem: Three problems. (1) DECOMPOSITION: the scope defines the ledger's return as {..., headcount, cleanTax, ...} and defines taxTake() as round(pop*rate*0.28 + jobs*rate*0.18) + cleanTax, while lastBudget.taxes INCLUDES cleanTax (js/sim.js:5185-5187). So on any clean-industry city 'headcount === lastBudget.taxes' is false by exactly cleanTax — the gate contradicts the ledger shape the same scope defines, and gate 2(b) simultaneously insists cleanTax must be included. (2) VACUOUS AS RUN: MEASURED isCleanInd() === false on the pinned reference city at tick 600, so the 20-seed x 600-tick run never exercises cleanTax at all — the sub-gate passes trivially either way. (3) TIMING TRAP: if assessedLedger() re-measures rather than reading the committed _dparts snapshot, it CANNOT hit 0 mismatches — the source already documents this exact hazard for demandBreakdown (js/sim.js ~4245: recomputeDemand runs at the top of tick() and growthPass then moves pop/jobs underneath it, 'measured divergence up to 0.34'). And a re-scanning ledger called every rollover by the gate's own harness perturbs the scan count gate 2(c) measures.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Split it: '(a1) ledger.headcount + ledger.cleanTax === lastBudget.taxes at every rollover across 20 seeds — 0 mismatches; (a2) the same identity on >=10 purpose-built clean-industry cities where cleanTax > 0 — 0 mismatches; (a3) assessedLedger() is specified to read the committed _dparts snapshot, never a fresh census, and gate 2(c)'s scan count is measured with the ledger harness detached.'

gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[2] — SEPARABILITY ('raise ONLY the industrial rate by 6 points ... built iJobs falls >=12% vs control while resTiles and pop each stay within 4%')
gate_problems.problem: MEASURED response of built iJobs to a demand.i shift of the size a +6 industrial-rate move produces (taxMod*0.4 = -0.12): global rate 7 -> 2,016 iJobs; rate 11 -> 2,008 (-0.4%); rate 12 -> 1,960 (-2.8%); rate 13 -> 1,600 but with pop simultaneously -20% (4,584 -> 3,680) because the whole city has gone over the cliff. Below the cliff the industrial response is ~3%, far short of 12%; at and above the cliff nothing is separable at all (pop moves as much as iJobs). Under the current curve no industrial-only rate move produces >=12% iJobs decline with pop within 4%. Because the gate is also written to 'pass either way', the practical effect is that the milestone's headline feature (per-zone rates) can never ship, and the gate cannot fail to reveal that — the decision is buried inside a gate that always passes.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Separate the decision from the gate. Gate: 'publish the separability measurement (iJobs / resTiles / pop vs an identical control at +120 rollovers, 20 seeds) in docs/gp7-spike.json — bar: numbers present.' Decision rule stated outside the gate: 'three sliders ship only if iJobs falls >= X% with pop and resTiles within Y%.' Set X from the measurement (the current physics supports roughly 3% at +6 points, so either X must drop or the rate delta must be much larger), and run it AFTER the taxMod reshape, since the reshape is the only thing that can move this number.

gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[3](a) — 'cumulative funds delta over rollovers 360-600 stays within +/-10% of zero'
gate_problems.problem: '+/-10% of zero' is zero — the denominator is undefined, so the bar is either literally unachievable (exact zero drift over 240 months) or unstated. There is no reference quantity named: 10% of the mean monthly take? of funds at the window start? of cumulative revenue over the window? MEASURED for scale: the pinned reference city at 7% ends 600 ticks with funds 440,865 from a 200,000 start and lastBudget.net +11,825/month, so the quantity being bounded is large and the choice of denominator changes the bar by orders of magnitude. (Compounded by the rollovers-vs-ticks problem above.)
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: '|funds(end) - funds(start)| <= 0.10 x (sum of realized monthly take over the same window)', with start/end stated in TICKS (e.g. ticks 360..600 of the pinned protocol), measured on city.funds, 20 of 20 seeds inside the band.

gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[3](c) — 'The floor is observed to bind: monthly take > 0 on every rollover while >=1 developed tile remains — bar: 0 zero-revenue months across 20 seeds x 600 ticks'
gate_problems.problem: The pinned corpus never goes near zero revenue — MEASURED take on the reference city at 7% is 13,211/month with 964 developed tiles, and the sub-gate's title claims the floor is 'observed to bind' while the measurement can only observe that a healthy city has positive revenue. Every build, floor or no floor, passes. The only measured configuration where take approaches zero is rate 0 (take exactly 0) or the post-collapse city at rate 20 (pop 0, 4 developed tiles, take 115) — neither is in the gate's fixture.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Add an adversarial fixture that actually reaches the floor: 'bulldoze/blight the pinned city down to N developed tiles (and separately set taxRate 0) and assert monthly take > 0 on every rollover while >=1 developed tile remains, and assert take === 0 the rollover after the last developed tile is removed' — so the floor's boundary is what is observed, not a healthy city's solvency.

gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[4] — CALIBRATION AND SCENARIO SAFETY ('this build wins on >= as many corpus_seeds as baseline for every scenario')
gate_problems.problem: Scenario cities are NOT seeded by the corpus: each SCENARIOS entry pins its own seed in source (gridlock-97 971104, twister-season 51996, blackout-summer-97 970601, y2k-ready 990704; js/scenarios.js:67 'new City(o.seed, 80)'). There is no corpus_seed axis to count wins over, so 'wins on >= as many corpus_seeds' is uncountable as written. The established harness varies k = 0..9 (the scripted reference solution at scratchpad/gp1b-scenario-ref.mjs jitters placements and slider timing by k), which is the axis the earlier '>= 8 of 10 seeded playthroughs' bar referred to. The gate's calibration clause also consumes 'the GP6 baseline's mean monthly take over rollovers 480-600', a number nothing in GP7a produces (GP7a's spike publishes tick-600 point values).
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'For each of the four scenarios, run the pinned scripted solution at k = 0..9 on this build and on the pinned GP6 baseline worktree (:8902). Bar: this build wins on >= as many of the 10 playthroughs as baseline for every scenario, and 0 scenario-k pairs regress.' And have GP7a's spike publish the 7% take as a mean over the same window GP7b calibrates against, so the calibration reference exists on the unchanged build.

gate_problems.gate: GP7a quality_gates[1] — 'a numeric elasticity (d revenue / d term at the equilibrium point) for BOTH taxMod and jobsAvail/220 ... Measured on the unchanged build'
gate_problems.problem: taxMod is parameterised (vary taxRate), but jobsAvail/220 (js/sim.js:4184/4228) has NO knob: it is a derived census term, so 'd revenue / d term' for it cannot be measured on an unchanged build without injecting an offset — which is a modified build, contradicting the gate's own 'measured on the unchanged build' clause. The two elasticities are also not commensurable: taxMod enters demand.r/c/i with weights 1 / 0.6 / 0.4 while jobsAvail/220 enters only demand.r. MEASURED, the honest answer the gate is groping for is not an elasticity at all: at the reference equilibrium jobsAvail/220 = 2.51 against clampD's ceiling of 1.0 (js/sim.js:1788), so demand.r is SATURATED and taxMod's full |0.65| swing moves residential demand by exactly 0 for every rate from 0 to ~13. An elasticity number would report 0 for taxMod and be undefined for the other term, hiding the actual finding.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Replace the elasticity pair with a directly measurable saturation report: 'for each rate 0..20 publish the PRE-CLAMP raw demand.r/c/i and the clamp headroom, and state at which rate each bar leaves the clamp — bar: raw values and clamp flags present for all 21 rates x 20 seeds, plus a one-line verdict naming the binding term and the rate at which it starts binding.'

gate_problems.gate: GP7a quality_gates[5] — 'history.assess present in BOTH js/sim.js:31 and js/sim.js:5274; after 300 rollovers all 11 series have equal length — bar: 0 length mismatches'
gate_problems.problem: The gate does not say WHICH city. On a fresh city it passes. On a LOADED mature v17 save it cannot: the trim at js/sim.js:5273-5275 fires on this.history.pop.length > 240 and then shifts EVERY key, so a save whose history is already at the 240 cap pushes assess to 1 and immediately shifts it back to 0 on every rollover — history.assess stays permanently EMPTY, forever, and the lengths never equalise. The save_version_plan's claim that a v17 save 'loads with assess=[] and records forward (the M30 idiom)' is therefore false for any city older than 240 months. (Note 600 ticks = 25 rollovers, so this state needs ~5,760 ticks or a long-played save — it will be found by a player, not by the gate.)
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the fixture and add the migration: '(i) fresh city, 300 rollovers: all 11 series equal length; (ii) a v17 save whose history is at the 240 cap, loaded and run 30 rollovers: history.assess is non-empty and all 11 series are equal length' — which forces normaliseHistory (or the load path) to left-pad a newly added series to the incumbent length instead of relying on push-forward.

gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[6](b) — 'a screenshot-diff of starved vs funded is non-empty at all 4 rotations'
gate_problems.problem: A non-empty screenshot diff is not evidence of anything in this renderer: the scene carries animated, time- and RNG-dependent content (trains, smoke plumes at js/render.js:1568 gated on Math.random, choppers, ticker text), so two captures of the SAME state also diff non-emptily. The bar passes for a build in which starved and funded urban renewal render identically.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Make it a controlled comparison: 'capture starved vs funded from the same tick with animation frozen (or diff only the deterministic budget-dialog chip region and the inspector text): bar - the chip class and label strings differ, and the map/inspector readout for a starved tile differs from a funded one by >=60 in two RGB channels at cam.r 0/1/2/3, while a same-state capture pair diffs by 0 pixels in the same region.'

gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[7](d) — 'mean per-tick wall time and budget-dialog slider-drag latency each within 110% of HEAD'
gate_problems.problem: No repetition count, no warm-up, no variance discipline, and no statement of which machine or which city — headless wall-time in this container swings well over 10% run to run, so the gate can fail (or pass) on noise while the code is unchanged. GP7a's gate 2(c) already demonstrates the deterministic alternative (an instrumented count of full-length over[] iterations).
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Gate on deterministic operation counts plus a loose timing sanity band: 'instrumented count of full-length over[] passes per tick, and per drag of a funding slider, equals HEAD exactly (deptCosts adds no per-tile pass); AND median per-tick wall time over 5 runs x 600 ticks after one warm-up run is within 125% of HEAD measured in the same session.'

gate_problems.gate: GP7a quality_gates[6] — 'grep for the 0.28/0.18 coefficient pair across js/ — bar: 1 hit, in js/sim.js'
gate_problems.problem: The grep is not well defined and fails for unrelated reasons as literally written. '0.28' alone currently hits js/sim.js:4229, :4267 and :4280 (the demand.c shopper term and its breakdown rows), plus js/render.js, js/sprites.js and js/audio.js; and the advisors doc comment the same gate wants corrected writes the constants as '.28' / '.18', which a '0.28' grep misses entirely. A worker can also pass the bar trivially by hoisting the literals into a named constant.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'Exactly one LINE in js/ matches the regex 0\\.28[^\\n]*0\\.18 (the pair on one line), and it is in js/sim.js; and exactly one line matches \\(7 *- *[a-zA-Z.]*[Tt]axRate\\) *\\* *0\\.05. Doc comments may restate the formula only by naming taxTake()/taxMod, never by repeating the literals.'

missing_coverage: taxTake() as scoped has NO rate parameter, but advTaxesAt(rate) is called with the OLD rate at js/advisors.js:403 (advTaxesAt(O) vs advTaxesAt(N)) to compute the projected revenue loss. GP7a gate 2(b) only tests advTaxesAt(city.taxRate), so a delegation that ignores the argument passes every gate while making `loss` identically 0 and printing 'a projected §0 a month gone' in the Transportation advisor's protest. Needs a gate: advTaxesAt(r) for r in 0..20 on >=10 states equals a city-independent recomputation at rate r (including cleanTax scaling with r), not just at the live rate.

GP7b cutover has no gate retiring GP7a's PREVIEW framing: the budget block is shipped in GP7a labelled 'Assessed valuation (not charged)' (js/ui.js:1103-1150). After the cutover that label is a lie on screen and the GP5b 'incl. High-tech premium' row's relationship to the new bill is unstated. Needs an S4 gate on the post-cutover budget dialog text and on the preserved js/ui.js:1131-1132 row.

GP7b(6) TRANSIT IN RENT is the milestone's headline player-facing promise ('rail finally shows up as rent') and is a declared RNG re-pin (landv -> gFit at js/sim.js:1079), yet no gate measures it: nothing isolates railCov's contribution to landv, nothing shows it in the wealth-band map or inspector at 4 rotations, and no outcome gate compares realized take for a rail-served vs identical rail-less pinned city.

GP7b(5) 're-tie upkeep to SERVED LOAD by CONSUMING deptStrain/approvalCensus, never a second definition of load' is unmeasured. Gates cover perf and the surplus band but nothing asserts the bill and the strain meters agree — e.g. deptCosts' load inputs are bit-identical to the popLoad/jobLoad/structures and roadTiles/jam/jamShare the meters display, on the same tick, across 20 seeds.

Per-zone rates have no gate on the GP6 surfaces that read the SCALAR c.taxRate: APPROVAL_TERMS 'tax' row (js/sim.js:1645-1649, both the pen() penalty and the blurb) and js/advisors.js:192-199's three branches. Approval is an EMA carry that IS serialized, so an undefined/NaN taxRate there poisons persisted state permanently. Needs: approval finite and the survey/advisor strings free of 'undefined'/'NaN' under per-zone rates, across 120 rollovers and a save round-trip.

Nothing certifies the READOUT against the ledger. GP7a gate 2 proves assessedLedger() agrees with the bill, and gate 4 proves the minimap bands render, but no gate ties the numbers rendered in fillBudgetTable's preview (per-sector projected take R/C/I and the delta) to assessedLedger()'s {assessed.r/c/i, headcount} fields — the UI could print a differently-derived number and pass every gate.

GP7b gate 6(c) (credit-rating downgrade fires exactly once) has no fixture guaranteeing a downgrade occurs: on the pinned corpus the reference city runs a permanent surplus (measured funds 200,000 -> 440,865 over 600 ticks at 7%), so a 600-tick run may never downgrade and the '1 message per transition' bar is vacuous. Needs a scripted forced-downgrade (and forced-upgrade) fixture.

No gate covers the interaction between the new assessed FLOOR and the equilibrium-revenue curve at rate 0: with a floor, take is no longer 0 at 0% tax, which changes what 'revenue at 0%' means in gate 2 and creates an unattended-income path the no-free-surplus gate measures only at the calibrated rate. Either gate revenue at rate 0 explicitly, or state that the floor is rate-scaled.

gate_problems.gate: GP8a — HONEST ODDS AT THE CALIBRATION POINT vs GP8a — BAND RESPONSE WITHIN ONE ROLLOVER
gate_problems.problem: These two gates cannot both pass, and the contradiction is forced by GP8a's own BYTE-IDENTICAL SIM gate. Because GP8a provably does not move the sim, the true hazard rate on EVERY city is the constant 1-(1-0.0009)^288 = 22.84%/yr and the true per-kind split is the fixed ladder at js/sim.js:5481-5487, independent of fire coverage, police funding, plant age or coastline. Scope item 3 puts the band chip AND the live per-year odds figure on the same row, derived from the same row score. So either (a) the published odds are constant across cities — the honesty gate passes but it is a single-point identity, the band chip can never move, and BAND RESPONSE fails 0/4; or (b) the odds vary with city state so the bands move — BAND RESPONSE passes, and the honesty gate then fails on every soak city that is not the calibration reference, because four bands spanning Low/Elevated/High/Severe imply an odds spread far wider than ±20% relative. The scope text half-concedes this ('normalised so that a documented REFERENCE CITY sits exactly on those shipped odds') but the gate measures '10 seeded 50-year soaks', not the reference city. This is the same shape as the y=12/y=9/y=15 incident: the fixture cannot produce the measured quantity.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Split the claim in two. (i) CALIBRATION-POINT IDENTITY (GP8a): on the ONE documented reference city, hazardReport().pTick equals 0.0009 to 1e-9 and the seven row weights equal the shipped ladder to 1e-9 — an exact analytic assertion, no soak needed. (ii) MONOTONIC RESPONSE (GP8a): the four scripted interventions each move their own row's SCORE strictly in the documented direction and cross at least one band boundary. Move the empirical ±20% honesty measurement entirely to GP8b, where the sim actually follows the ruler. Additionally: on GP8a the panel must not print a per-year odds figure that varies by city while the sim's rate does not — either print the odds only on the reference calibration, or label the varying number as 'exposure', which is what it actually is on this half.

gate_problems.gate: GP8a — HONEST ODDS: 'the measured per-kind shares are each within ±20% relative of the panel's per-kind odds'
gate_problems.problem: Statistically unachievable by construction at the specified sample size. 10 soaks x 50 years = 500 city-years; at 22.84%/yr that is ~114 total events. Monster is 1.5% of the ladder => expected 1.7 events across the WHOLE experiment; riot 5.5% => ~6.3; flood 7% => ~8. A Poisson count with mean 1.7 has ~77% relative standard deviation. To hold the monster share inside ±20% relative at 95% confidence you need ~96 monster events, i.e. ~6,400 total events, i.e. ~28,000 city-years — 56x the specified budget. The gate will fail on a perfectly correct implementation on most seed sets, and passing it once would be luck. Only the fire row (~63 events, ~13% rel. sd) is even marginally powered.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Either (a) assert the per-kind split ANALYTICALLY rather than empirically — hazardReport()'s seven normalised weights equal the shipped ladder constants (.55/.13/.10/.08/.07/.055/.015) to 1e-9 — which is exact, free, and actually proves the thing; or (b) keep the empirical form only for the AGGREGATE rate and for kinds whose expected count over the horizon is >= 30, and explicitly exclude kinds below that floor from scoring, reporting their observed counts instead. The same fix is needed on GP8b's 'CALIBRATION BAND + THE RULER STAYS HONEST', which re-runs the identical per-kind ±20% test at the identical 500-city-year budget.

gate_problems.gate: GP8a — MENU REACHABILITY: 'MENUS.disasters() returns exactly 7 kind rows plus the Random Disasters toggle (length === 8 counting the separator per the live shape)'
gate_problems.problem: Off-by-one against the live shape the gate claims to be counting. js/ui.js:372-379 today is [fire],[tornado],[UFO],"-",[toggle] = 5 elements: 3 kinds + 1 separator + 1 toggle. Going 3->7 kinds gives 7 + 1 separator + 1 toggle = 9, not 8. An implementer who ships the correct menu fails the assertion and will be tempted either to drop the separator (a real UI regression, losing the divider between the destructive rows and the toggle) or to quietly amend the bar — exactly the S6 failure this role exists to prevent.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'MENUS.disasters() returns 9 elements: 7 kind rows, one "-" separator, and the Random Disasters toggle — asserted as (rows.filter(r => Array.isArray(r)).length === 8 && rows.filter(r => r === "-").length === 1), so the count is robust to future separator placement.'

gate_problems.gate: GP8a — HONEST ODDS: '...within ±20% RELATIVE of the odds the panel publishes for those same cities'
gate_problems.problem: The soak cities are never specified, and the sim makes the choice load-bearing in two ways the gate does not survive. (1) COASTLINE: startDisaster('flood') aborts at js/sim.js:4645 ('if (!front.length) return') without counting on a landlocked map, so the measured flood share is exactly 0 there while the shipped ladder publishes 7% — a relative error of 100%, and the aggregate rate also falls ~7% below the 22.84% analytic. On a coastal map neither is true. (2) POPULATION: the roll is gated on 'pop > 200' (js/sim.js:5477), so any soak that starts from a small town spends its opening years at a rate of 0, dragging the 50-year mean below the analytic reference. Neither 'coastal or landlocked' nor 'pop trajectory' nor 'is the panel expected to publish flood=0 on a waterless map' is pinned, and the answers change whether the gate passes.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pin the fixture in the gate text: 'over 10 seeded 50-year soaks on the SAME documented coastal 80x80 city script (city = new City(seed,80), funds 1e9, tier 4, pop held above 200 from tick 0 — asserted), ...'. And state the required panel behaviour explicitly: 'on a landlocked city the panel must publish flood odds of exactly 0 and renormalise the remaining six rows to the aggregate — asserted directly, not measured by soak.'

gate_problems.gate: GP8a — S4 ROTATION + FAILURE-STATE DISTINCTNESS: 'the Risk minimap mode produces an identical per-tile band buffer at cam.r 0/1/2/3 (0 differing tiles after the documented rotation mapping)... verified on screenshots at all 4 rotations'
gate_problems.problem: The minimap does not rotate, by explicit design, so this clause is trivially true for any implementation including a broken one. renderMinimap (js/render.js:2243) never reads cam.r; the code comments say so twice — 'stays north-up like every other minimap mode' at the dist branch, and 'Reads planes only — north-up, never cam.r.' near the end of the function. There is therefore no 'documented rotation mapping' for the minimap to apply, and the phrase invites an implementer to go looking for one that does not exist (the second incident's failure mode). Four screenshots of a north-up buffer prove nothing.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Drop the rotation clause from the minimap gate and state the real invariant instead: 'the Risk minimap is north-up like every other mode — assert renderMinimap's risk branch reads no cam.r (grep: 0 occurrences of cam.r inside the branch) and that the painted buffer is byte-identical at cam.r 0/1/2/3.' Keep the genuinely useful half unchanged: MM_NAMES has 14 entries, updateMapLegend returns a non-empty name+swatch for 'risk' with no stale caption, and the four band colours are 4 distinct hex values distinguishable by lightness as well as hue (the GQ11 deutan rule the other ramps follow). Note the real S4 rotation risk in GP8 lives in GP8b's dispatch sprites, where the gate is already correctly written.

gate_problems.gate: GP8a — NAMED CONTRIBUTOR IS THE ARGMAX: 'the driver string the panel names equals the argmax of that row's own driver list in 200/200 cases'
gate_problems.problem: 'argmax of the driver list' is undefined over the drivers the scope actually specifies, because they are in incommensurable units: fire coverage 0..255, police funding 0..100 (percent), plant age in years vs PLANT_WARN_AGE=40, pollution and crime on their own index scales. The declared row shape is {id,label,val,blurb} — an argmax over raw `val` would name 'fire coverage 200' over 'funding 30%' purely because 255 > 100, which is a genuinely wrong claim to the player, and the gate as written would certify it. Separately, in its current form the gate is close to a tautology: it re-derives the same argmax from the same table the panel used, so it can only catch a display-wiring bug, never a modelling error.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'Each driver row carries a NORMALISED contribution field (0..1, its share of the row score, documented per driver) alongside its raw val; the panel names the argmax over that normalised field, ties broken by the documented id order. Across 200 scripted states spanning the ranges, the named string equals that argmax in 200/200. Additionally, on 12 hand-labelled single-cause states (only one driver moved off its healthy value) the panel names THAT driver in 12/12 — the half of the gate that can actually fail.'

gate_problems.gate: GP8a — BAND RESPONSE: 'and no unrelated row changes band in the same window (0 spurious band changes)'
gate_problems.problem: A zero-tolerance absolute on a shared census. Every one of the four interventions moves quantities that feed every row: bulldozing fire stations changes deptStrain's fire cap AND its structure count (js/sim.js:4970-4990); setting funding.police to 0 changes polCov and, via recomputeMaps within 14 ticks, the crime plane that the riot row reads and the land-value chain other rows read; zoning 20 coastal tiles changes popLoad/jobLoad the moment any lot develops. Any row already sitting near a band boundary will flip on that shared movement — and the gate gives no rule for how far from a boundary the fixture must start. This is an unbounded-flakiness bar with no relationship to whether the ruler is correct.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Make it directional and comparative rather than absolute: 'each intervention moves its own row's SCORE by >= 2x the largest score change of any other row in the same window (4/4), and no other row's score moves in the direction that would be reported as worsening.' If a band-crossing assertion is wanted, state the fixture precondition: 'the test city is scripted so every row's score starts at least 25% of a band width from its nearest boundary — asserted before the intervention.'

gate_problems.gate: GP8a — ONE BUGLE PER KIND: '20 launches per kind => exactly 20 entries per kind'
gate_problems.problem: newsQueue is a consumed queue, not an accumulator. newsFrame (js/ui.js:2097-2102) runs every frame from the main loop and shifts one entry off whenever #dlg-news is not open. Under any harness that lets the render loop run — which is the normal way this repo is driven, and is required by the same gate's 'invoking each row' clause going through the live menu closure — the queue will hold 0 or 1 entries, never 20, and the gate fails on correct code. Nothing in the gate says the loop is stopped or that pushes rather than residents are counted.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'Instrument the push site: wrap city.newsQueue.push and count calls. 20 scripted launches per kind produce exactly 20 push calls per kind (140 total), 7 distinct headline strings, 0 duplicate headlines across kinds, and every pushed entry is an object with non-empty headline/sub/body (never a bare number — newsFrame at js/ui.js:2101 dispatches on typeof ed === "number" to showNewspaper, so a numeric push would render as a tier promotion).'

gate_problems.gate: GP8b — DIFFICULTY AXIS IS REAL AND TWISTER-SEASON IS UNMOVED: 'the generalized path fires tornadoes on exactly the same set of elapsed months as the pinned GP8a baseline across 20 seeds (0 differing spawn months, 0 differing medal tiers)'
gate_problems.problem: Unachievable by construction, and it directly contradicts GP8b's own declared re-pin. The shipped schedule at js/scenarios.js:369-371 is guarded by '&& !c.disaster' — whether a scheduled tornado fires in a given month depends on whether a random misfortune happens to be active at that moment. GP8b replaces the probability at js/sim.js:5477 with a coupled pTick and re-weights the kind ladder, which changes both WHICH months carry an active disaster and the rng.hazard cursor position (each startDisaster consumes 4 rh.next() draws; the per-tick gate consumes 1). disastersEnabled defaults to true (js/sim.js:2017) and no scenario disables it, and Twisterton's scnBuildTown population clears the pop>200 gate, so random misfortunes definitely fire during the scenario. Therefore the set of elapsed months on which tornadoes fire MUST differ under any real coupling. Medal tier is downstream of months-left-at-win, which is downstream of how much development the extra/fewer disasters destroyed — so '0 differing medal tiers' is doubly unreachable. This is the exact shape of incident #1: a bar unreachable by construction and unrelated to the work.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Split the semantic claim from the byte claim. (i) SEMANTICS, asserted directly: 'the generalized pressure path, evaluated on twister-season's shipped {type:"tornado", everyMonths:2, months:12} config with the random-misfortune roll suppressed (disastersEnabled=false), fires on exactly the same elapsed-month set as the pinned baseline under the same suppression — 0 differing months — and sc.pressure defaults, medals {gold:18,silver:9} and winTarget 4000 are unchanged by grep.' (ii) OUTCOME, comparative per R1: 'with disasters enabled, twister-season run on this build vs the pinned GP8a baseline across 20 seeds: it still wins on every seed it won on baseline, and no medal tier regresses.' Never assert bit-for-bit month equality across a declared re-pin.

gate_problems.gate: GP8b — DISPATCH AGENCY: 'the allowance computed from deptStrain is strictly smaller than the burning front at its peak in >= 90 of 100'
gate_problems.problem: Unit mismatch — the two sides of the comparison are not the same kind of quantity, and no conversion is documented anywhere in the spec. deptStrain's cap (js/sim.js:4986) is powered_fire_anchors x SVC_DEF[OV.FIRESTA].cap x funding/100, and SVC_DEF fire cap is 240 STRUCTURES COVERED (js/sim.js:1405). A modest city with 5 powered stations at 100% funding yields cap = 1200. The 'burning front at its peak' is a count of tiles with fire[i] > 0 — typically tens, since fireTick decrements by up to 3/tick with the cov>40 bonus (js/sim.js:4534) and fire[] is seeded at 8-17. So 'allowance strictly smaller than the front' is systematically FALSE by two orders of magnitude, in essentially 0 of 100 samples rather than 90. The gate is only measurable once the spec documents the mapping from deptStrain's structure-capacity number to a dispatch UNIT COUNT — and that mapping is the actual design decision this gate is supposed to be policing.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Document the derivation in the scope and gate it as one formula: 'units = floor(deptStrain().fire.cap / DISPATCH_UNIT_LOAD) with DISPATCH_UNIT_LOAD a named frozen constant; the gate asserts units < (count of tiles with fire[i] > 0 at the fire's peak) in >= 90 of 100 sampled fires, and that DISPATCH_UNIT_LOAD is chosen so this holds — i.e. the scarcity is a designed constant, stated, not an emergent hope.' Also reconcile the player_facing_win, which promises the allowance is ALWAYS smaller, with the gate's 90/100.

gate_problems.gate: GP8b — DISPATCH AGENCY: 'city.dispatch.length === 0 within one tick of this.disaster becoming null or fire[] emptying, in 100/100 sampled events'
gate_problems.problem: Read as the disjunction it is literally written as, this gate forbids dispatch from ever existing during a fire — which is the milestone's headline mechanic. startDisaster('fire') sets fire[] and returns at js/sim.js:4607 WITHOUT ever assigning this.disaster; the split spec itself notes this fact in its save_version_plan. So during every fire, this.disaster is already null, the first disjunct is permanently satisfied, and the assertion demands city.dispatch.length === 0 at all times. Fire is 55% of the ladder, so this covers the majority case. The intent is obviously a conjunction, but an implementer running the gate as written fails on correct code — the second incident's failure mode verbatim.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'city.dispatch.length === 0 within one tick of the city becoming quiet, where quiet is defined as (this.disaster === null AND no i with fire[i] > 0) — asserted in 100/100 sampled events. Separately, dispatch units targeted at a disaster that ends while units are still alive are cleared in the same tick the disaster clears (100/100), and a unit whose ticks reach 0 is removed on that tick regardless of city state.'

gate_problems.gate: GP8b — COUPLING OUTCOME OVER A HORIZON vs A CONTROL: 'at matched population (within ±5%)'
gate_problems.problem: Circular and unstated as to when it is measured. Arm B is deliberately neglected — no fire coverage, 0% police funding — which in this sim suppresses growth through the certified GP5a/GP5b chain (svcStrain multiplies stampCoverage potency, crime suppresses land value) AND, under the very coupling this gate is measuring, destroys developed tiles to fire and riot. So the intervention under test is precisely what breaks the matching condition, and the tighter the coupling works the further apart the populations drift. The gate does not say whether ±5% is checked at tick 0, at the end, or as a horizon mean, and the three give different verdicts. Left as written this becomes either an unsatisfiable precondition or a silently-reinterpreted one.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Normalise instead of matching: 'measured as successful startDisaster(kind) counts PER 1000 POPULATION-YEARS, integrating population over the horizon rather than requiring the two arms to end at the same size. Report both arms' population trajectories. Arm A's fire rate per 1000 pop-years is >= 50% below arm B's, and arm A's riot rate >= 70% below arm B's.' If a matched-population design is genuinely wanted, pin it as a scripted-and-frozen footprint: both arms build the identical zoned footprint from the same script and growth is not the variable under test.

gate_problems.gate: GP8b — COUPLING OUTCOME: 'arm A suffers ... >= 70% fewer riots than arm B'
gate_problems.problem: Noise-dominated at the specified horizon, and — unlike the difficulty-axis gate in the same list — it carries no minimum-event floor. Riot is 5.5% of the ladder; at the baseline 22.84%/yr that is ~1.26%/yr, i.e. ~0.63 riots per 50-year run and ~6 riots for arm B across all 10 runs. Coupling will raise arm B's number, but plausibly only into the teens. Requiring a >= 70% reduction against a denominator of order 10 means one or two lucky events flips the verdict. The very next gate in the same list gets this right ('both >= 5 events so the ratio is not noise'), so the omission here is inconsistent within the milestone.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Add the same floor and widen the horizon for the rare kinds: 'arm B accumulates >= 20 riots over the horizon (extend the number of seeded runs until it does, reporting the count) before the ratio is scored; then arm A's riot rate is >= 70% below arm B's.' Or drop riot from the numeric bar and gate it directionally — 'arm A's riot rate is strictly below arm B's in >= 8 of 10 paired seeds' — which is measurable at this sample size.

gate_problems.gate: GP8b — CALIBRATION BAND: 'arm A's aggregate annual disaster rate is <= 23%/yr'
gate_problems.problem: Trivially satisfied: 23%/yr is the CURRENT uncoupled rate (1-(1-0.0009)^288 = 22.84%/yr), so a build that does nothing whatsoever for arm A passes this clause, as does the GP8a baseline itself. It carries no information about whether the coupling helps a well-run city. The paired '>= 1.5x' clause is doing all the work; this half is a decorative absolute where the meaningful statement is comparative, which is exactly the pattern R1 exists to forbid.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'Arm A's aggregate annual disaster rate is at least 25% BELOW the GP8a baseline arm run on the same seeds and the same build script (i.e. good governance measurably buys safety, not merely the status quo), and arm B's is >= 1.5x arm A's.'

gate_problems.gate: GP8b — COUPLING OUTCOME: 'with arm B's rate also re-measured against the GP8a baseline arm to prove the effect is coupling and not a global rate cut'
gate_problems.problem: No pass/fail criterion is attached. 'Also re-measured' names a measurement but never states what value would fail it. As written the clause can be satisfied by simply reporting a number, which means the anti-global-rate-cut protection — the whole reason the clause exists — is unenforceable.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'arm B's aggregate rate is >= the GP8a baseline arm's rate on the same seeds (a neglected city is never made SAFER by the coupling), and arm B's fire rate is strictly greater than baseline — so a uniform reduction in pTick cannot pass this gate.'

gate_problems.gate: GP8b — DETERMINISM + PERF: 'The hazard vector is computed <= 1 time per 24-tick rollover and 0 times per frame (call counter)'
gate_problems.problem: Contradicts GP8a, which this milestone builds on. GP8a's Risk minimap mode and #dlg-civdef panel both consume hazardReport(), and renderMinimap is driven from js/main.js:72 on a per-frame timer ('if (++mmCounter % 15 === 0) renderMinimap(city, UI.mapMode)') — i.e. roughly 4x/second whenever Risk is the selected mode. A naive call counter on hazardReport will therefore show many calls per second while the Risk view is open, failing '0 times per frame' on a correct implementation. The gate never distinguishes the sim-side hazVec computation from UI-side reads of the same pure function.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'Count only the SIM-side consumer: city.hazVec is assigned at most once per 24-tick rollover and never inside tick()'s per-tick body or any render path — asserted by a counter on the assignment site, not on hazardReport() itself. Separately assert that UI-side hazardReport() reads never write city state (serialize() byte-identical across 1000 Risk repaints, per GP8a's ZERO-DRAW gate).'

gate_problems.gate: GP8b — SCENARIO WINNABILITY, COMPARATIVE (R1): 'months-left-at-win regresses by <= 2 months on any winning scenario'
gate_problems.problem: No seed or run count is specified, uniquely among GP8b's gates (every other one names 10, 20 or 100 samples). Since GP8b is a declared re-pin, a single scripted run per scenario is pure seed noise — the same script on the same build with a different seed can easily swing months-left by more than 2. The gate's structure is correct per R1; only its sample size is missing, which is enough to make it either flaky or accidentally lenient depending on the seed the implementer happens to pick.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: '...run the same scripted solutions on this build and on the pinned GP8a baseline across 20 seeds per scenario. No scenario that wins on baseline on a given seed loses on this build on that seed; no medal tier regresses on any seed; and the MEDIAN months-left-at-win across the 20 seeds regresses by <= 2 months on any winning scenario.'

missing_coverage: GP8a has NO performance gate at all, yet it ships an O(n) census on a per-frame timer. The Risk minimap mode is repainted from js/main.js:72 ('if (++mmCounter % 15 === 0) renderMinimap(city, UI.mapMode)') roughly 4x/second, and the per-tile band buffer needs hazardReport, which per the scope does a full coast-front scan plus City.deptStrain() (both O(map)). Worse, GP8b's perf gate is measured 'within 5% of the GP8a baseline' — so any regression GP8a introduces is baked into the baseline and never caught by either half. Needs a GP8a gate: mean frame time and _jaComp/_jaNC cache-hit rate over a 600-tick soak with the Risk minimap selected are within 5% of the pre-GP8a pin, and the risk band buffer is recomputed at most once per repaint (memoised on a sim revision counter, the terrRev/powerEpoch idiom).

GP8a's new ADVISORY_GATES row (FIRE_RISK_HIGH) has no gate that it ever fires, or that it stays quiet on a healthy city. A predicate that is never true is vacuously byte-neutral and passes every gate in the GP8a list — the byte-identity gate cannot tell a correct advisory from dead code. The GP5a precedent (POLICE_THIN / FIRE_THIN, js/sim.js:1758-1774) is the model. Needs: on a scripted thin-coverage city, diagnoseTile(i).advisories contains FIRE_RISK_HIGH on >= 1 tile with the documented evid rows populated; on a scripted healthy city it appears on 0 tiles.

GP8a's item 8 — 'optional auto-pause + camera jump on disaster start, behind a UI.prefs flag' — has no gate whatsoever, and it is the ONE item in GP8a that changes what the running game does when a disaster lands. It also adds new persisted state outside the save file (UI.prefs via savePrefs) with no round-trip gate. Needs: with the flag off, disaster start leaves UI.paused and cam.x/y/z/r unchanged (byte-neutral to the running session); with it on, exactly one pause and one camera jump per disaster start, not per tick; the pref survives a savePrefs/reload round-trip and defaults to the documented value when absent from localStorage.

GP8a adds four new Snd voices (quake/flood/riot/monster, js/audio.js:60-67 today holds only siren/boom/ufo) with no distinctness gate. S4's 'every failure state must be visually distinct from its working state' has an obvious audio analogue here — seven disasters sharing three voices is exactly the failure the milestone is fixing. The ZERO CONSOLE ERRORS gate only proves the four new voices do not throw. Needs at minimum: the 7 kind rows map to 7 distinct Snd functions (asserted by identity, not by ear), and each new voice's documented waveform/envelope parameters differ from all six others.

GP8a's Civil Defense 'Show me' buttons have no gate that they land on the right thing. The gate list covers the mode switch machinery (setMapMode / MM_NAMES / no stale caption) but nothing asserts that a row's focus function returns a tile that actually carries the named driver — and unlike GP6's survey, all seven focus functions are NEW here. Needs: for each of the 7 rows on a scripted city, focus() returns an in-map index, and for the rows with a spatial driver (fire coverage, police coverage, plant age, coastline) that tile is in the documented worst decile of the corresponding plane.

GP8b: the history-series double-key-list rule has no gate. The scope correctly names both sites (normaliseHistory js/sim.js:31 and its mirror in the >240 trim loop at js/sim.js:5274) and the substrate notes flag it as a repeat failure, but the requirement is stated conditionally ('If a monthly risk/disaster-rate history series ships') and no quality gate enforces it. Needs, conditional on shipping a series: the new key appears in BOTH hardcoded lists (grep asserts 2 occurrences); a save/load round-trip preserves the series (normaliseHistory does not drop it); and after >240 months the series is trimmed to the same length as every sibling series.

GP8b has no S4 gate on the coupled RATE itself — only on dispatch sprites. The player is told a band moved, but nothing gates that the world visibly reflects the changed exposure, and every visibility gate in the milestone sits on GP8a's panel, which was calibrated against a DIFFERENT (uncoupled) model. Needs: after GP8b lands, the Risk minimap and the panel band chips on a neglected city read materially worse than on a well-run city of comparable size — asserted on screenshots at the two arms — so the S4 expression tracks the coupling rather than the frozen GP8a calibration.

GP8b: the flood O(n^2) cost that the scope explicitly warns about (item 6: d.flooded.indexOf(ni) at js/sim.js:4768/4779) is not gated. The perf gate measures 'mean frame time over a 600-tick soak', which at even an elevated hazard rate will rarely contain a large flood at all, and mean frame time hides a spike anyway. Needs: worst-case tick time during a scripted maximum-extent flood is within a documented bound of the GP8a baseline's equivalent flood, and peak serialize() size during that same scripted flood grows by <= 5% (the existing clause, but paired to a SCRIPTED flood rather than to whichever flood the coupled model happens to produce, which is not a paired comparison).

GP8b: the M29 'no phantom count on a waterless map' invariant is named in scope item 7 but never gated against the coupled model. The coupled vector changes how often flood is picked, and the abort path at js/sim.js:4645 returns before recCur.disasters++ — so a re-weighting that routes more rolls to flood on a landlocked city silently changes the Almanac's 'Disasters Survived' column relative to the number of events the player actually experienced. Needs: on a landlocked 80x80 soak, recCur.disasters equals the count of disasters that actually started (0 phantom counts), and the panel's published flood odds on that city are 0.

gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 7 (S4 VISIBILITY): "#mapmodes.scrollWidth <= #mapmodes.clientWidth (no horizontal overflow at the 160px cap, css/style.css:220-225)"
gate_problems.problem: MEASURED FALSE ON THE PRE-GP9a BUILD, with zero GP9 code. I served the repo on :8901 and read the live box: #mapmodes has 13 .mm buttons, gridTemplateColumns resolves to "34px 34px 34px 34px 34px 34px 34px" (7 tracks), scrollWidth = 244, clientWidth = 160. The strip ALREADY overflows by 84px. It is designed to: css/style.css:220-225 sets grid-auto-columns: minmax(34px,1fr) with a hard width:160px and overflow-x:auto, and the shipped comment on that rule says in terms "width: 160px; /* hard cap = minimap width: the strip scrolls, never grows */". The gate demands the opposite of the shipped design contract, and no correct GP9a implementation can satisfy it — this is incident #1 repeating exactly (an absolute bar the baseline already fails, unrelated to the work).
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Replace with the comparative form that actually expresses the intent (the 14th button must fill the existing 7th column's empty second-row cell rather than open an 8th column): "#mapmodes contains exactly 14 .mm buttons; #mapmodes.scrollWidth is UNCHANGED from the pre-GP9a build (measured 244 today) and #mapmodes.offsetHeight is unchanged (still exactly two rows); getComputedStyle(#mapmodes).gridTemplateColumns still resolves to 7 tracks."

gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 7 (S4 VISIBILITY): "the four captures are PIXEL-IDENTICAL to each other (the minimap is north-up by contract, js/render.js:2249)"
gate_problems.problem: MEASURED FALSE ON THE PRE-GP9a BUILD at every non-degenerate camera position. renderMinimap paints the tiles north-up, but then strokes a camera-viewport rectangle over the same canvas (js/render.js:2362-2381) whose bounds come from screenToTileF at the four screen corners — and the shipped comment there says explicitly "route the four screen corners through the rotation-aware FLOAT inverse ... so the box bounds the ROTATED visible region in tile space at every rotation". I hashed the full 160x160 minimap ImageData at cam.r 0/1/2/3 on four camera configs (z=1 centred, z=2 at 20,20, z=2 at 60,15, z=4 centred): all four configs produced FOUR DIFFERENT hashes. (The bar passes only at a degenerate clamped camera — cam.x=0, cam.y=1280 — which is why it looks plausible.) The cited authority, js/render.js:2249, is the `dist`-mode comment "stays north-up like every other minimap mode", which covers the TILE PAINT only and says nothing about the overlay stroke the gate's measurement includes. This is incident #2's shape: the gate's own justification does not cover the quantity it measures, and the implementer would burn a full cycle proving the gate wrong.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Measure the tile paint, not the whole canvas: "the four captures are PIXEL-IDENTICAL to each other after masking the camera-viewport stroke (compare ImageData with pure-white #ffffff pixels excluded), OR capture with the camera pinned to a fully-zoomed-out, map-clamped position where the projected box is rotation-invariant by construction — state which, and pin cam.x/cam.y/cam.z in the harness."

gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 8(iii): "all 5 scenarios in js/scenarios.js (gridlock-97, twister-season, blackout-summer-97, y2k-ready, +1) ... the 5-element pass/fail vector is identical or strictly better"
gate_problems.problem: js/scenarios.js contains exactly FOUR scenarios. SCENARIOS = [ at line 91, closing ]; at line 286, with ids at lines 93 (gridlock-97), 139 (twister-season), 183 (blackout-summer-97) and 233 (y2k-ready). There is no fifth. The gate's "+1" placeholder and its "5-element pass/fail vector" cannot be produced by the fixture. Everything else about this gate is correct and is the right R1 comparative construction — the count is the only defect, but it makes the bar literally unmeasurable as written.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: "all FOUR scenarios in js/scenarios.js (gridlock-97, twister-season, blackout-summer-97, y2k-ready) ... the 4-element pass/fail vector is identical or strictly better." Re-read the array at launch rather than pinning the count from the spec, since GP7/GP8 precede GP9 and may add rows.

gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 4 (Σ CONTRACT) and GP9b gate 6 (S4): "mix.waste equals the summed rated MW of POWERED incinerator anchors EXACTLY" / "a POWERED incinerator (plume + lit) vs an UNPOWERED idle one is > 5% distinct at all 4 rotations"
gate_problems.problem: Nothing in the declared design can ever set powered[] on an incinerator tile, so both bars are pinned at the failing value by construction. Three mechanisms light a tile in recomputePower: isPlant() self-lights and seeds the flood (js/sim.js:2381-2383); isMega() self-lights as a power island (2394); and the flood enters a neighbour only if conducts(j) (2367-2369, 2402). GP9b's declaration table explicitly EXCLUDES OV.INCIN from conducts() and states it does NOT join isPlant() (the COLLISION 2 decision), and it is not isMega. The only remaining precedent — the PUMP terminal-receiver loop at js/sim.js:2435-2450 — is gated on `this.over[i] !== OV.PUMP` and GP9b declares the incinerator EXCLUDED at that site too ("pump-feed (2435) excludes both"). Result: powered[incinAnchor] === 0 forever, mix.waste === 0 forever, and there is no reachable "powered incinerator" art state. The scope gestures at this once — "the PUMP precedent ... which also proves the 2x2 anchor + power-receiver pattern" — but the eight-site membership table, which is what gate 3's 16/16 asserts, never declares a receiver rule, and gate 3 conflates the two senses of the 2435 site (which tiles may FEED a pump vs which tiles are ENERGIZED as receivers).
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Add a NINTH declared site and gate it: "OV.INCIN is energized by a terminal-receiver pass mirroring the PUMP loop at js/sim.js:2435-2450 — non-propagating, run after the brownout/y2k cuts, anchor lit iff any tile orthogonally touching its 2x2 footprint is powered and is itself a real conductor." Then gate 3 becomes 18/18 (9 sites x 2 ids) and gate 4 should add: "an incinerator with no wire run to it reads powered[anchor] === 0 and contributes 0 to mix.waste; the same incinerator with a wire run reads 1 and contributes its full rated MW." If instead the incinerator is meant to generate unconditionally, delete the word "powered" from gate 4 and drop gate 6's powered/unpowered pair.

gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 1 (STREAM -> OVERFLOW): "city.cityIndex(city.poll) rises by >= 20 from tick 0"
gate_problems.problem: cityIndex is a whole-MAP mean (js/sim.js:5283-5287: sum over all 6400 tiles / 6400, wilderness included), and the project has already MEASURED and DOCUMENTED its reachable ceiling. js/sim.js:1516-1517 states, in the GP6 fix-pass block that exists precisely because someone else made this mistake: "measured ceiling of cityIndex(poll) with the ENTIRE map converted to coal plants is 40, and cityIndex(crime) sat at 5 with every patrol defunded ... 12 + 8 points of weight were dead." A rise of >= 20 on that index therefore demands that garbage overflow from a 300-tile city (4.7% of the map) generate HALF the citywide pollution of a map paved wall-to-wall with coal plants. No sane calibration of a backlog-scaled source reaches that, and pushing a constant until it does would wreck every other pollution-coupled bar. This is the same class of failure GP6 already had to repair, one file over.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Two independent fixes, either or both: (a) measure over the INHABITED footprint the way GP6's approvalCensus does rather than the whole-map mean, and (b) make it comparative against the control instead of absolute — e.g. "the zero-disposal arm's mean poll over the zoned footprint exceeds the drained control's by >= 15 at rollover 24, and the gap widens monotonically over the final 12 rollovers." Pin the threshold against a measured reachable range, not against the 0..255 type range.

gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 1 (STREAM -> OVERFLOW): "while the control's [cityIndex(poll)] drifts by < 3"
gate_problems.problem: This is an absolute bar on the CONTROL arm's own behaviour over 24 rollovers, and the control is a living, growing city — it develops zones, its industry levels up (js/sim.js:3669 emits (30 + lvl*35) per ZI tile), its roads accumulate traffic and its plants load up (coalSmog scales 40 -> 160 with powerDemand/powerSupply at js/sim.js:3718-3721). None of that has anything to do with waste. A control that simply grows can easily drift more than 3 index points and fail a gate about garbage. Same defect as the first incident: a bar that measures something other than the work.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Delete the control-side absolute and state the whole thing as one difference: "the zero-disposal arm's pollution index exceeds the drained control's by >= X at rollover 24, where both arms ran the identical seed and script." The control's own drift then cancels out of the measurement instead of becoming a failure mode.

gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 1: "history.waste (the series GP9a certified) is non-decreasing over all 24 [rollovers]" — in the ZERO-DISPOSAL arm
gate_problems.problem: The same gate requires this arm to be poisoned by its own garbage (rising pollution) while simultaneously requiring its waste OUTPUT never to dip — but waste output is a pure function of over[]/lvl[], and the sim de-levels developed tiles under exactly the conditions this gate is trying to induce. The decline paths: applyDecline at js/sim.js:1121-1123 (`c.lvl[i]--` on a demand-driven draw), the UNPOWERED decay at 1135, and the gridlock decay at 4464 (`if (this.lvl[i] > 1 && gCong(...) > 0.8 ...) this.lvl[i]--`). Rising poll[] drives landv[] down (js/sim.js:3731, `- this.poll[i] * 0.7`), which drives gFit down, which drives demand down, which drives applyDecline. Over 24 rollovers a genuinely overflowing city can lose levels and its tonnage can fall — the gate then fails BECAUSE the feature worked. Monotonicity of the stock (garbageBacklog) is safe; monotonicity of the flow (history.waste) is not.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Keep the strictly-increasing backlog bar (that one is sound — with zero disposal the stock only accumulates) and restate the flow bar comparatively and with slack: "history.waste at rollover 24 is >= its value at rollover 1, and the zero-disposal arm's history.waste is element-wise >= the drained control's at every rollover" — or drop it entirely, since garbageBacklog strictly increasing already proves the stream is live.

gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 5 (CROSSTALK AUDIT IS A TRUE MIRROR): "34 x 8 = 272 boolean comparisons, 272/272 identical, 0 mismatches"
gate_problems.problem: Seven of the eight hoisted predicates are pure functions of the overlay byte and mirror cleanly. The eighth, ovIsStructure, is NOT — so for 4 of the 34 ids the "value the pre-GP9a build's inline expression produced for that id" does not exist, and the gate cannot be evaluated. At the census (js/sim.js:4966-4981) the control flow is: `if (t === OV.NONE) continue;` (NONE is not a structure, but NONE is not in SVC_LINEAR, so the natural hoist `!SVC_LINEAR.has(t)` returns TRUE for it — a guaranteed mismatch); then `if (t === OV.ZR || t === OV.ZC || t === OV.ZI) { const l = this.lvl[i]; if (!l) continue; structures++; }` — for the three zone ids the site's answer depends on lvl[i], not on t, so there is no single boolean to compare against. 4 of the 272 cells are ill-defined and will read as failures on a correct hoist.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Either carve the ambiguity out explicitly — "ovIsStructure(t) is defined as `t !== OV.NONE && !SVC_LINEAR.has(t)`, and the comparison is run over the 30 NON-ZONE ids only (30 x 8 = 240 assertions); the three zone ids' structure membership is lvl-dependent and is asserted separately as `lvl > 0` at both a lvl-0 and a lvl-2 tile" — or split the site into ovIsStructure(t) for non-zone ids plus an explicit ovZoneIsStructure(t, lvl). Restate the total (240 + 6, or whatever the split yields) so the arithmetic in the bar matches the assertions actually run.

gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 4 (THE POWER PIE STOPS LYING), the S6 finding: "the count of those 6 in which the PRE-GP9a build's displayed total differs from city.powerSupply (expected 4 — every configuration with a live deal)"
gate_problems.problem: The expected count is 3, not 4, and the reasoning behind "every configuration with a live deal" is wrong for one cell of the matrix. powerTradeDelta (js/sim.js:4373-4384) computes `const sold = Math.min(sellCommit, Math.max(0, plantSupply - demand)); return buys - sold;`. In the sell x DEFICIT configuration, plantSupply < demand by definition, so `Math.max(0, plantSupply - demand)` is 0, sold is 0, buys is 0, and the delta is EXACTLY 0 — powerSupply equals the plant sum and the pre-GP9a displayed total does NOT differ. Only sell x surplus, buy x surplus and buy x deficit produce a nonzero delta. A worker who dutifully records "3" against a gate that says "expected 4" is forced either to escalate or to quietly amend the bar.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: "...the count of those 6 in which the PRE-GP9a build's displayed total differs from city.powerSupply (expected 3: sell x surplus, buy x surplus, buy x deficit — sell x deficit is provably delta-0 because powerTradeDelta caps sold at max(0, plantSupply - demand), js/sim.js:4381)." Note the 6/6 exact-equality bars themselves are sound: the Math.max(0, ...) clamp at js/sim.js:2382 is unreachable, since sold <= plantSupply always.

gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 8 (PERF: NO REGRESSION ON EITHER PATH): "200 x deptStrain() within 5% ... 200 x recomputePower() within 5% ... a full 600-tick run within 3%", median of 5 runs
gate_problems.problem: The tolerances are tighter than the instrument. I measured the noise floor on a saturated 76x76 city in the harness Chromium: 200 x deptStrain() = 5.2 ms median, raw runs 4.9 / 5.0 / 5.1 / 5.1 / 5.2 / 5.2 / 5.2 / 5.6 / 5.8 — an 17.3% spread and ±9% around the median. 200 x recomputePower() = 8.9 ms median, raw runs 8.9 ... 12.0 — a 34.8% spread. Both timed blocks are single-digit milliseconds, so timer granularity and JIT tiering dominate; a median-of-5 does not shrink that to 5%. The 3% bar on a full 600-tick run is worse, because it compares across two separate browser contexts against two separate servers (:8901 vs :8902). This gate will pass or fail on scheduler luck, which is exactly the state that invites a worker to re-run until it passes.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Size each timed block above the noise floor and widen the tolerance to something the instrument can resolve: "20,000 x deptStrain() and 5,000 x recomputePower() (each block >= 200 ms), median of 9 runs, within 10% of baseline; a full 600-tick run, median of 9, within 8%." Better still, add a noise-floor control: run the SAME build against itself first and require the observed self-vs-self spread to be below the tolerance before the cross-build comparison is admitted as evidence.

gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 6 (SAVE ROUND-TRIP): "a save whose history.waste holds 250 entries survives load AND is trimmed in lockstep — all ELEVEN history arrays equal length after the next rollover"
gate_problems.problem: As written the fixture cannot produce the measured quantity. The trim (js/sim.js:5273-5276) is `if (this.history.pop.length > 240) for (const k of [...]) this.history[k].shift();` — a single shift per rollover, guarded on POP's length, not on each key's. A save in which only history.waste holds 250 entries loads with pop at whatever the other ten hold; if that is <= 240 the guard never fires, nothing is trimmed, and waste stays at 250+1 while the others sit at N+1 — the eleven are unequal on a perfectly correct implementation. Even with all eleven at 250, one rollover pushes one and shifts one, so they end at 250 each, equal but not "trimmed" to 240. The bar's intent (both key lists were extended) is right; its fixture and its success condition are not.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the fixture and split the two claims: "(a) a save in which ALL ELEVEN history arrays hold 250 entries loads, and after the next rollover all eleven are still equal in length and all eleven shrank by exactly the same amount — proving the collectBudget trim list at js/sim.js:5274-5276 was extended; (b) a save whose history object contains a `waste` key loads with that key preserved and non-empty — proving normaliseHistory's list at js/sim.js:31 was extended (an unextended list silently drops it to [])."

gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 2 (THE TWO ROUTES GENUINELY DIFFER): arm "(B) landfill sized to zero the backlog" vs arm "(C) incinerator of equal rated tonnage", both required to "hold garbageBacklog === 0 for the final 24 rollovers" of 120
gate_problems.problem: The two arms are sized in incommensurable units, so "equal rated tonnage" cannot be satisfied for both. The incinerator is a FLOW (fixed tonnage consumed per rollover, per the scope's monthly waste tick) and needs only rate >= monthly tonnage. The landfill is a STOCK (per-cell `fill`, saturating, per GP9b gate 5's own saturation bar) and to hold backlog at 0 through rollover 120 it must have capacity >= the CUMULATIVE 120 months of tonnage in a city that is also growing. A landfill "of equal rated tonnage" to the incinerator saturates and arm B fails; a landfill sized to survive 120 rollovers is not "equal" to the incinerator by any reading. The gate as written guarantees one arm fails, and the failure is about the fixture, not the build.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Name the two sizings separately and drop "equal": "(B) a landfill field whose TOTAL capacity exceeds the cumulative 120-rollover tonnage by >= 20%; (C) an incinerator bank whose per-rollover RATED TONNAGE exceeds peak monthly tonnage by >= 20%." Keep the backlog === 0 bar on both. If a like-for-like comparison is wanted, add a separate short-horizon arm (24 rollovers) where the landfill is genuinely rate-matched, and gate on the saturation date instead.

gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 3(i) and GP9b gate 5: "toggling `recycle` cuts wasteCensus().total by the DESIGNED PERCENTAGE +/-2%"
gate_problems.problem: "The designed percentage" is not a number in the spec — it is whatever value the implementer assigns to the recycle row's wasteMul at implement time. The bar therefore cannot fail in its design dimension: an implementer who picks wasteMul 0.95 passes the gate exactly as easily as one who picks 0.70, and the gate certifies nothing about whether Recycling is a meaningful player choice. The ±2% slop is doing real work (it catches per-tile vs total rounding drift in the fold at js/sim.js:4302-4313), but the percentage itself is self-referential.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pin the constant in the spec before launch so the bar is falsifiable: "the recycle row carries wasteMul: 0.75; toggling it cuts wasteCensus().total by 25% +/-2%." S6 note: the constant is a tuning knob and may be re-argued at launch, but it must be a NUMBER in the gate, not a forward reference to the implementation.

gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 7 (S4 VISIBILITY): "the image is non-black and non-uniform (>= 8 distinct pixel values)"
gate_problems.problem: WASTE_RATE is declared as a FROZEN per-zone-type x per-level table (3 types x 3 levels = 9 possible non-zero rates), and the minimap is declared to paint wasteRateAt(i) per tile directly. The number of distinct colours the canvas can carry is therefore bounded by the number of distinct (type, level) pairs actually PRESENT in the fixture, plus the background/water/dim-context colours and the white viewport stroke. A city with ">= 100 developed zone tiles" — the only fixture condition the gate states — will typically be mostly lvl 1-2 residential with some commercial and light industry, i.e. 3-5 distinct rates. 3 rates + background + water + white stroke = 6 distinct values on a completely correct build. The bar assumes a continuous ramp over a plane; it is being applied to a 9-valued lookup.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Tie the threshold to the fixture instead of guessing at it: "the count of distinct non-background pixel values equals the count of distinct (zone type, level) pairs present in the fixture, and that count is >= 4 — pin the fixture to contain at least ZR lvl 1, ZR lvl 3, ZC lvl 2 and ZI lvl 2 so the bar has something to count." Keep the non-black / non-uniform bars as-is.

gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 4 (Σ CONTRACT): "with a sell deal open on a city whose ONLY generation is incinerators, city._tradeSold > 0"
gate_problems.problem: The fixture is under-specified in a way that can fail a correct build. js/sim.js:4381 computes `sold = Math.min(sellCommit, Math.max(0, plantSupply - demand))`. On a city whose only generation is incinerators, the quantity passed as plantSupply is the incinerator MW (that is the point of injecting it before the call at js/sim.js:2382) — so _tradeSold is 0 whenever the city's own demand meets or exceeds the incinerator output, no matter how correctly the injection was implemented. The gate states no relation between incinerator MW and demand.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: "...on a city whose ONLY generation is incinerators AND whose powerDemand is strictly less than the incinerator bank's rated MW, with sellCommit <= (ratedMW - demand): city._tradeSold === sellCommit exactly." The exact-equality form is strictly stronger than "> 0" and pins the injection point unambiguously.

gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 2 (THE RULER IS HONEST AND MONOTONE): "total is strictly monotone non-decreasing across the five (4/4 pairwise)"
gate_problems.problem: Two issues. First, "strictly monotone non-decreasing" is internally contradictory — strict monotonicity and non-decreasing are different predicates and the gate does not say which is being asserted. Second, whichever is meant, the bar cannot fail on any correct implementation: WASTE_RATE is a frozen table of non-negative rates, wasteCensus is a plain sum over tiles, and the five cities are a nested sequence (0 / 40 / 120 / 300 / 600 developed tiles from the same script). More tiles of non-negative rate means more total, by construction. It certifies nothing the Sigma cross-check bar in the same gate does not already certify. The level-sweep bar (>= 2.0x) in the same gate IS real — it constrains the table's shape — and should be kept.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Either drop the monotonicity bar as vacuous, or replace it with something that constrains the design: "total per developed tile stays within a 3x band across the five cities (the ruler must not be dominated by one zone type), AND the ind:res ratio of wasteCensus() exceeds 1.5 at every one of the five (industry heaviest, per the M31 design the scope cites)." Also fix the wording to a single predicate.

missing_coverage: S4 VISIBILITY — the garbage GRAPH SERIES is ungated. GP9a ships history.waste plus a UI.graphSeries entry (js/ui.js:33) plus a checkbox in index.html, and GP9b gate 1 measures its whole overflow curve against that series, but NO gate opens the graph dialog, ticks the checkbox and asserts a plotted line appears. Gate 7 covers only the minimap and gate 4 only the pie. Because the series ships `on: false` per the GP3a/GP6 default-off policy, a broken checkbox wiring or a missing seriesData path (js/ui.js:1522-1534) is invisible to every gate in the split — the exact 'nothing invisible ever bills the player' failure S4 exists to catch. Suggested bar: with the checkbox ticked at all three graph ranges (1yr/10yr/100yr), the garbage line renders non-empty and its final plotted value equals the last element of city.history.waste.

S4 VISIBILITY — the PER-TILE garbage readout in the query panel is ungated and arguably undelivered. GP9a's rationale claims 'a query row' as one of four player-facing wins, but the six numbered deliverables in scope do not include a query-panel waste row, and no gate asserts one. GP9b gate 5 asserts only the literal string 'full' for a saturated landfill cell. If the minimap is the sole per-tile expression, wasteRateAt has no numeric surface anywhere.

GP9b's new COMPLAINT kind `garbage` has NO gate of any kind — not that it fires, not its text, not the tile it targets, and not the scope's own claim that 'it changes which x,y the ticker jumps to ONLY in cities carrying a backlog'. This matters concretely: the declared score is `40 + backlogPressure` where backlogPressure is a CITYWIDE scalar, so every tile scores identically, and scanComplaints picks the winner with a strict `score > bestScore` (js/sim.js:5328) — meaning the garbage complaint always resolves to the LOWEST map index that qualifies, and the ticker's 'Show me' camera jump lands on the same corner tile every single time. Nothing in the split would detect that. Suggested bars: the complaint fires within COMPLAINT_EVERY*2 rollovers of the backlog crossing its threshold; its (x,y) is a landfill/high-waste tile rather than index 0; and on a zero-backlog city the complaint kind and target are byte-identical to the GP9a build's.

GP9b's ADVISORY_GATES WASTE_OVERFLOW row is ungated. The scope adds it 'so diagnoseTile explains the stall', which is the GP1a substrate contract, but no bar asserts city.diagnoseTile(i) actually emits the row on a stalled tile in a backlogged city, nor that it stays absent on a clean one. Draw-neutrality is covered (gate 8(ii)); presence and correctness are not.

The REPAIRED POWER PIE has no rendering gate. GP9a gate 4 checks the legend TOTAL string only. Nothing asserts the new SIGNED trade row renders correctly when the value is negative (an export), that fillPowerMix's arc loop at js/ui.js:1080-1085 does not emit a negative or NaN sweep when a trade row is folded in, or that the pie still draws when total <= 0. GP9b adds a SIXTH `waste` slice with the same gap — gate 4 checks mix.waste numerically but nothing checks the slice renders or that POWERMIX_TYPES was extended (the scope itself warns 'omit the row and the pie silently under-sums').

GP9b gate 5 measures with `city.wasteCapacity()`, an instrument that neither half's scope declares or ships. Under S3 the behavior half must be measured by instruments the read half certified; wasteCapacity() cannot live in GP9a (fill[] does not exist yet), so it must at minimum be named as a GP9b deliverable with its own definition, or the gate is measuring with a ruler that appears for the first time inside the gate that uses it.
