GP9b gate 8(ii)'s attribution claim overreaches, and the residue is ungated. With WASTE_RATE zeroed and a GP9a-era scripted build order (which by definition cannot place a landfill or incinerator — those tools do not exist in GP9a), the two new over[] ids never appear in over[], so the eight predicate edits, the five tool registries (COST/TOOL_TIER/OV_SIZE/toolOverlay/TOOLS), the budget line and the complaint kind are NEVER EXERCISED by that run. Byte-identity therefore cannot 'prove' they contribute no drift — it proves only that dormant code is dormant. Gate 3 part 2's live probes do cover the eight predicates with a real landfill field; the tool registries, the deptCosts/collectBudget/lastBudget-ctor budget line and the complaint kind have no equivalent probe. Suggested addition: a WASTE_RATE-zeroed run that DOES place landfills and an incinerator, byte-identical to itself across load/save and asserting funds delta equals exactly the placement cost plus upkeep.

No save-compat bar covers the GP9a ordinance plumbing on a LEGACY save. GP9a adds `wasteMul: 1` to identityOrdMods (js/sim.js:632-634) and a fold line to recomputeOrdinances (4302-4310). A pre-GP9a save with `recycle` already enacted must reload with ordMods.wasteMul defined rather than undefined — recomputeOrdinances is documented as running on load, so this is probably safe, but gate 6 asserts nothing about ordMods at all. One bar: 'a pre-GP9a save with recycle enacted loads with typeof city.ordMods.wasteMul === "number" and wasteCensus().total finite and non-NaN.'

GP9b determinism gate 8(i) reproduces history.waste, garbageBacklog and history.poll across 20 seeds but omits fill[] — the other new serialized array. Gate 7 compares fill[] on a load-vs-native run, but the 20-seed determinism sweep does not, so a seed-dependent divergence in landfill fill ordering would only be caught if it happened to perturb the backlog.

gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 5 (BLIGHT RADIATES) — crime clause
gate_problems.problem: "mean crime in the 4-tile annulus is >= 10 HIGHER than control" is unreachable under the scope's own design. Crime is NEVER diffused: the only diffuse() calls in recomputeMaps are poll (sim.js:3681), land value (3694) and traffic (3700). Crime is a pure per-tile formula, `density - polCov - landv*0.2 - ordMods.crimeCut` (sim.js:3746-3748). The scope puts the blight crime term inside that per-tile loop gated on aband[i], so a NON-abandoned annulus tile receives blight crime only through the landv channel at coefficient 0.2 — a +10 crime annulus requires a -50 landv annulus, i.e. more than three times the gate's own -15 landv bar. No constant choice fixes this; the term simply does not reach the annulus.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Split the measurement to match where each term actually applies: measure crime ON the abandoned cluster tiles (where the added term lives) and landv on the annulus (which the diffused pollution channel does reach). If crime is genuinely meant to radiate, that is a SCOPE change — seed a diffused blight source in the source loop at sim.js:3663-3681 (the `if (this.fire[i]) src[i] += 100` idiom) feeding a diffused plane, and re-derive the annulus bar from the diffusion kernel rather than asserting a number.

gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 3 (COUNTER EXACTNESS) — the 168/544 = 0.309 clause
gate_problems.problem: The gate hardcodes "distressShare holds constant at 168/544 = 0.309", citing sim.js:5049-5059. Two problems. (1) WRONG METRIC: those numbers are unpowShare (zoned tiles that are dark), recorded in prose at sim.js:1590-1592 and 5054-5057. distressShare counts ALL FOUR causes, so it is >= unpowShare by construction — cutting power to a third of the city also crashes sector demand, so SLUMP fires on tiles DARK does not cover and the share cannot equal 0.309. (2) NO FIXTURE: repo-wide, 544/168/0.309 appear ONLY inside those two comments. There is no committed script or save that reproduces that city, and it was measured on a build that HAD abandonment (that is the bug the comment describes) — a build GP10a by definition is not. The literal is not reproducible.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Make it a co-measurement instead of a literal. (a) distressShare must be NON-DECREASING across 24 consecutive rollovers with the wire still cut — the actual anti-self-healing property. (b) The DARK-cause subset count (tiles with distressCause === DARK+1) must equal approvalCensus's live zUnpow on the same city at the same rollover, exact integer equality, every rollover — this proves the shared denominator without importing a number. (c) If a fixed number is wanted, commit the scripted city as a fixture and re-measure it on the GP10a build first.

gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 3 (HYSTERESIS)
gate_problems.problem: Scope §6 defines revival as "an abandoned tile needs REVIVE_W consecutive rollovers at distress == 0 before the ABANDONED row stops matching." The gate then measures revival latency against REVIVE_W with a ±2 tolerance on >= 18 of 20 runs, plus "EXACTLY 0 tiles revive before rollover REVIVE_W - 2". Both clauses are true by construction — the latency IS REVIVE_W, exactly, because a counter is being compared to its own constant. The gate tests that a decrement works, and the ±2/18-of-20 statistics create the false impression that something stochastic is being measured. It cannot fail without the feature being outright broken.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Replace with the exact identity (latency === REVIVE_W on 20 of 20, zero tolerance — cheaper and strictly stronger), and move the real content into a comparative assertion the constant does NOT trivially satisfy: a DESIGNATED renewal district's revival latency is shorter than an undesignated one by exactly the designed reduction, on the same seed and the same cluster, 10 of 10 pairs. Also assert the distress counter is genuinely re-armed — a tile that hits distress > 0 mid-window restarts at 0, it does not resume.

gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 4 (CAUSE ATTRIBUTION IS EXACT)
gate_problems.problem: The two clauses cannot both be met with the stated tolerance. Every tile with distress[i] > 0 got there because SOME DISTRESS_CAUSES row matched (first-match, scope §3), so its distressCause is necessarily one of the four rows. If "each of the other 3 rows [is reported] on 0 tiles", then the target row is on 100% of distressed tiles — the ">= 95%" allowance is unusable. An implementer who measures 96% has already failed the second clause, and will not know which clause is the real bar. This is the same shape as the y=12/y=9/y=15 incident: the fixture described cannot produce the quantity measured.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pick one bar. Either: "100% of distressed tiles report the target row and the other 3 rows appear on 0 tiles" (clean, and what the fixture actually implies); or, if the single-cause city cannot be made that clean, ">= 95% report the target row, and the report ENUMERATES the residual <= 5% by cause with a stated reason" — dropping the 0-tiles clause. Do not ship both.

gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 7 (CROSSTALK PREDICATES) assertion 1
gate_problems.problem: "Abandoning N tiles drops this.powerDemand by exactly N at sim.js:2367-2372" is false in the scenario that produces abandonment. The loop counts `if (this.powered[i] && t >= OV.ZR && ...) demand++` — a tile only contributes when it is POWERED. The primary abandonment path in this milestone is DARK (unpowered for ABAND_W rollovers), and those tiles already contribute 0, so the drop is 0, not N. The assertion is additionally perturbed by the `pdMult` activeMods multiplier and `powerTradeDelta` immediately below (sim.js:2374-2382), either of which breaks exact-N.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the precondition in the gate: run the assertion on a POWERED abandonment path (a CRIME- or SLUMP-caused cluster), with no `powerDemand` activeMod (pdMult === 1) and no regional power trade open, then assert the exact -N drop. Separately assert the DARK case explicitly reads -0 so the null result is recorded rather than mistaken for a bug.

gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 9 (SPIRAL SURVIVABLE)
gate_problems.problem: The re-specification correctly drops the GP7 floor clause and adds a comparative clause, but it LEAVES an absolute bar in front of it: "returns the city to positive monthly net AND rising pop within 60 rollovers on THIS build in >= 8 of 10 seeded runs". That is the exact shape of incident 1 ("wins the medal in >= 8 of 10"). It is also the clause most likely to fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the work: GP10b ADDS decline pressure (ABAND_SMOG pollution, blight crime, a landv subtraction, and the census exclusion removing taxable pop), so the absolute success count can legitimately fall below 8 while the comparative clause — the one that actually tests for regression — passes cleanly. Secondly, "rising pop" has no definition: rising measured over what window, against what point?
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Keep only the comparative clause: this build's success count >= the pinned pre-GP10 baseline's on the SAME script and seeds, with the per-seed outcomes tabulated. Report the absolute count as an OBSERVATION, not a bar. Define the success predicate concretely, e.g. "monthly net > 0 at rollover 60 AND pop at rollover 60 > pop at the trough rollover" — a single unambiguous headless read.

gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 1 (BOUNDED DECLARED RE-PIN)
gate_problems.problem: The gate's interesting half will almost certainly never execute. 600 ticks is 25 month rollovers (tick()'s %24 block, sim.js:5492). Reaching aband requires ABAND_W CONSECUTIVE distressed rollovers on top of the time to develop the city, so a normal scripted build on 20 seeds will very likely produce ZERO abandoning seeds. The gate then reads 20/20 byte-identical and PASSES, with the "first differing byte >= first aband[i]=1" clause — the entire point of the bounded re-pin — never exercised on a single seed. Nothing in the gate requires that any seed abandon.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Add a coverage precondition and make it a failure condition: the 20-seed script must include a deliberately sabotaged arm (power cut / service collapse) such that >= 6 of 20 seeds actually reach aband, and the gate FAILS if fewer than that number exercise the divergence clause. Report the abandoning-seed count in the results. Consider extending the horizon past 600 ticks for the sabotaged arm so ABAND_W + development time fits.

gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 2 (CAUSATION) — the 18-rollover / 60% bar
gate_problems.problem: ABAND_W is never given a value anywhere in the split spec, yet the gate hardcodes 18 rollovers and 60%. If ABAND_W > 18 the result is 0% by construction and the gate is unreachable. Worse, the denominator is ambiguous in a way that swings the answer from ~0% to ~100%: scope §1 says "a zoned tile with distress[i] >= ABAND_W flips to aband=1" with NO lvl guard, and scope §3 walks DISTRESS_CAUSES on any ZR/ZC/ZI tile regardless of level — so EMPTY zoned lots accumulate distress and abandon too, making >= 60% of the zoned footprint trivial. That directly contradicts two other statements: §1's "the tile KEEPS lvl[] so the derelict sprite has a size" (a lvl-0 abandoned tile has no size), and this gate's own separation clause "separates aband===1 from merely-decayed (lvl===0 && aband===0)", which presumes lvl-0 tiles do NOT abandon.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Declare ABAND_W in the scope and require 18 > ABAND_W with stated margin. Declare explicitly whether abandonment requires lvl > 0 (the derelict-sprite and separation clauses both imply it does). Then re-express the bar over the subset the answer is actually about: >= 60% of tiles that were DEVELOPED (lvl > 0) in the pre-cut snapshot, with the zoned footprint reported alongside as the stable denominator.

gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 6 (THE CAMPAIGN BEATS WAITING) — the 40%-fewer-rollovers clause
gate_problems.problem: "returns the cluster to within 5% of control mean landv at least 40% FEWER rollovers than the do-nothing arm" has no horizon and no censoring rule. The do-nothing arm is a blighted cluster with an abandonment feedback loop — the expected outcome is that it NEVER returns to within 5% of control. When the denominator is infinite/undefined the ratio is undefined and the gate can be neither passed nor failed honestly, which is precisely the condition under which an implementer quietly reinterprets the bar. (The second clause, ">= 25% more developed non-abandoned zoned tiles at rollover 60", is sound — it has a horizon.)
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Fix a horizon H (rollover 120 is consistent with the rest of the split) and define non-recovery as censored-at-H. Score the pair as a success when EITHER the renewal arm recovers by H and the do-nothing arm does not, OR both recover and the renewal arm's rollover count is <= 60% of the do-nothing arm's. Require >= 9 of 10 pairs and report the censoring split so "9 of 10 by censoring alone" is visible rather than hidden.

gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 5 (LEGIBILITY) — the distress complaint clause
gate_problems.problem: scanComplaints (sim.js:5314-5347) is a CITYWIDE winner-take-all argmax that emits at most one complaint per COMPLAINT_EVERY (= 3) rollovers. The shipped scores are flat: rubble 130, unpowered 150, traffic 60+excess, crime 40+excess, poll 40+excess. The natural way to produce "a district reaching >= 10 distressed tiles" is the DARK cause — which means >= 10 developed unpowered tiles, each scoring a flat 150. Unless the new distress kind scores ABOVE 150, no distress complaint can ever fire in that scenario, and the "within 2*COMPLAINT_EVERY rollovers" window contains at most two emission opportunities. If the implementer does score it above 150, the shipped unpowered and rubble complaints are starved — a regression the gate does not measure.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the distress kind's score RANK relative to the five existing kinds explicitly in the scope (it is a design decision, not an implementation detail). Run the timing assertion on a CRIME- or SLUMP-caused fixture where no higher-scoring kind co-occurs. Add a companion anti-crosstalk assertion: on a pinned pre-GP10a fixture, each of the five existing complaint kinds fires at its pre-GP10a rate over 120 rollovers.

gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 4 (CENSUS INTEGRITY) — the pop/jobs identity
gate_problems.problem: "city.pop === Σ RES_POP[lvl] over non-abandoned ZR and city.jobs === Σ COM_JOB/IND_JOB over non-abandoned ZC/ZI" is not the identity the code implements. computeDemandParts (sim.js:4163) also folds arcology contributions into the SAME totals: `else if (isArco(this.over[i]) && this.anc[i] === i) { pop += ARCO_POP[...]; iJobs += ARCO_JOB[...]; }` — a single Launch Arco adds 3000 pop. The stated identity therefore holds only on a city with no arcologies, i.e. it is an identity that passes on the toy fixture and silently stops being true on a real Megalopolis-tier city — exactly the failure mode this review is meant to catch. As written it could also produce a false FAIL if the harness happens to build one.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the full identity: pop === Σ RES_POP[lvl] over non-abandoned ZR + Σ ARCO_POP over arco anchors (anc === i), and the matching jobs form including ARCO_JOB. Then run it on a fixture that DOES contain at least one arcology, so the arco term is actually exercised rather than assumed absent.

gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 6 (S4 VISIBILITY) — the reference block
gate_problems.problem: The gate diffs a distressed block "against a pixel-identical healthy block". No such reference block can be constructed. Sprite variants are seeded per tile at growth time (`c.varnt[i] = rg.pick(5)` at sim.js:1115 and 1119) and at build time (sim.js:2270), terrain variants are seeded at generation (sim.js:2131-2132), and tiles are further differentiated by land value, pollution and neighbour context. Two distinct blocks on the same map are essentially never pixel-identical, so the gate has no constructible control and the implementer has no way to know whether a 2% diff came from the distress treatment or from varnt.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Diff the SAME tile against itself: capture at distress[i] = 0, then write the band value directly into the plane, re-render with camera, tick, funds and every other input held fixed, and diff. Repeat at cam.r = 0,1,2,3. That isolates the treatment exactly and needs no reference block. Keep the >= 2% threshold and the pairwise-band structure unchanged.

gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 7 (TEN-SITE CLEAR DISCIPLINE)
gate_problems.problem: "fire that site on a tile carrying distress >= 5" cannot be satisfied naturally at the road-crumble site (sim.js:3615). roadWearTick only touches OV.ROAD / OV.WIREROAD tiles, and distress is written ONLY on ZR/ZC/ZI (scope §3). The only route from a zoned tile to a road tile is place(), which passes through the footprint site at sim.js:2266 — a site this same gate requires to clear the planes. So no road tile can ever carry distress >= 5, and the precondition for that site is unconstructible. The gate reads as though all ten preconditions are naturally reachable, which will send an implementer hunting for a state that does not exist.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Say plainly that the harness WRITES distress[i] = 5 and distressCause[i] = k directly into the planes immediately before firing each site — this is a defence-in-depth clear test, not a reachability test. Additionally mark which of the ten sites are naturally reachable from a distressed zoned tile (2266, 2315, 4542, 4718, 4744, 4778, 4806, 4829, 2249) and which are defensive-only (3615), so a future reader does not mistake the defensive ones for live paths.

gate_problems.gate: GP10a scope §6 band thresholds (>= 6 / >= 12) vs GP10b gate 8
gate_problems.problem: GP10a pins the three visual bands at healthy / >= 6 / >= 12 and gates on them. ABAND_W is never assigned a value anywhere in the split. If ABAND_W <= 12, a tile flips to aband before it can be observed in the "critical" band, so once GP10b lands the critical band is unreachable state — and GP10b gate 8's requirement that abandoned tiles be "pairwise visually distinct from healthy AND from all three GP10a distress bands" contains a term that cannot be instantiated on a live city. The two halves' constants are coupled but only one of them is written down.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pin ABAND_W in GP10a's scope (not GP10b's) with ABAND_W > 12 and stated margin, OR define the bands as fractions of ABAND_W (e.g. >= ABAND_W/3 and >= 2*ABAND_W/3) so the two halves cannot drift apart. Then GP10b gate 8 can name the exact distress value it forces to observe each band.

gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 5 (BLIGHT RADIATES) — the -15 landv magnitude
gate_problems.problem: The -15 annulus landv bar is an absolute magnitude that was not derived from the code path that has to produce it. Scope §3 deliberately forbids seeding the blight penalty into lv[] (correctly — diffuse() clamps into a Uint8Array at sim.js:3768), so the fold term at 3730-3741 applies only to the abandoned tile itself. The ONLY radiating channel left into the annulus is `- this.poll[i] * 0.7` in the fold, meaning a -15 annulus mean requires roughly +21 diffused pollution there. Given diffuse(src, poll, 3, 0.24) over a 16-tile cluster, that implies an ABAND_SMOG well above the fire term's `src[i] += 100` (sim.js:3679). No pilot measurement is cited, so the bar may be reachable only with a constant that visibly outweighs an active fire.
gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Run a one-off pilot (place a 16-tile abandoned cluster, sweep ABAND_SMOG, read the annulus mean at +42 ticks) and PIN the bar to what the kernel actually yields at a defensible constant. Until then state it comparatively and directionally — "annulus mean landv is strictly lower than the matched control on >= 9 of 10 pairs, with the measured delta reported" — and add the magnitude bar once the pilot number exists.

missing_coverage: GP10b: the >= OV.ZR auto-join list is only PARTIALLY discharged. sim.js:347 enumerates the idiom sites as conducts / seed / demand / BROWNOUT / Y2K, and the live sites are demand (2370), brownout (2394), y2k (2410) and fire candidacy (4599). Scope §4 declares only demand + fire candidacy, and gate 7 asserts only those two. Nothing declares or asserts whether an abandoned tile is a brownout victim or a y2k victim — both read `this.powered[i] && t >= OV.ZR` and both will silently include abandoned tiles by default.

GP10a: no anti-crosstalk gate on the new `distress` complaint kind. scanComplaints (sim.js:5314-5347) is a single-winner citywide argmax with one emission per COMPLAINT_EVERY, so adding a kind can starve the five shipped kinds (rubble/traffic/unpowered/crime/poll) with no test noticing. Needs a pre/post firing-rate comparison on a pinned fixture over 120 rollovers.

GP10b: the ABANDONED row is placed in GROWTH_GATES after BURNING, i.e. BEFORE the shipped UNPOWERED row (sim.js:1131-1136). firstGate is first-match, so on an abandoned dark tile UNPOWERED's apply() no longer runs — the `c.unpow[i]` increment at 1134 stops and the `chance(0.35)` lvl-decay draw at 1135 stops. That is a behavior change to a shipped mechanic, and neither the scope's re-pin note (which mentions only sim.js:4461/4464) nor any gate covers it.

GP10b: the per-district `renewal` boolean is new PERSISTED state (it rides the districts[] round-trip at sim.js:5683 / 5785-5786). Gate 10 asserts sum(aband) === 0 on old saves but never asserts that a pre-GP10b districts[] record loads with the designation defaulting to false, nor that a DESIGNATED district survives serialize -> deserialize -> serialize with the flag and its § charge intact.

GP10a: gate 8 requires serialize -> deserialize -> serialize to be character-identical, but nothing establishes that this property holds on the PRE-GP10a tree. If the shipped round-trip is not already idempotent (key ordering through the Object.assign district restore, float formatting), the gate fails for reasons unrelated to GP10a and will burn a fix cycle. Measure the baseline first and record it.

GP10a: no cost gate on the new O(n) per-rollover sweep, despite distressTick calling trafficNear(i) per tile for the GRIDLOCK cause. The project precedent (recomputeJobAccess's _jaComp/_jaNC caching, explicitly flagged perf-critical) says per-tile rollover passes are cost-sensitive. Gate 2 counts visits but bounds no time.

GP10b: no S4/copy gate on the distress -> abandoned handoff. GP10a ships under an explicit HONESTY CONSTRAINT (no copy may promise abandonment) and GP10b's scope says it 'amends the copy to add the countdown', but no gate asserts the amended advisory text actually renders with the recovery countdown at the shipped surfaces (hover line, query verdict box, almanac) — gate 4 only checks v.evidence on diagnoseTile.
